cluster_summary: This cluster comprises vulnerabilities where file parsers fail to validate user-controlled integer values (offsets, sizes, counts) before using them in memory writes, loop bounds, or decompression. The lack of bounds checking allows attackers to trigger out-of-bounds writes, infinite loops, memory exhaustion, or CPU exhaustion via crafted files.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Clamp or reject excessive loop bounds; replace iteration over a range with iteration over actual collected object IDs..

mechanism.missing_guard: the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect
mechanism.name: Unvalidated loop bounds from input metadata causing CPU exhaustion
mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Clamp or reject excessive loop bounds; replace iteration over a range with iteration over actual collected object IDs.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Clamp or reject excessive loop bounds; replace iteration over a range with iteration over actual collected object IDs.
sub_patterns.name: Unvalidated loop bounds from input metadata causing CPU exhaustion
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled integer values from PDF stream or trailer dictionaries (e.g., /N, /Size) are used directly as loop bounds without validation or capping, allowing arbitrarily large iterations.
